rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 L5: "it runs"/"it exists" resolve same-sentence to "the hook"/"the script". Chunk 2 closest candidate is L15 "A menu, not a checklist." -- no explicit antecedent noun, but it is the immediate continuation of the prompt directly above it on the same chunk (the just-run demo's returned list), matching the rule's NOT-violation carve-out for "immediate continuation of the previous slide's subject". No never-named or vague-with-full-history referents found.

grep -inE 'opening lecture|earlier module|previous lecture|the prework' over body -> 0 hits. Closest candidate L11 "The same primitive covers everything else that must happen every time" stays same-file/same-chunk (refers to "hook" from the same bullet block, not a positional pointer at another file). Maintainer block's own file-provenance note (L19, L23) is maintainer prose, not body, and out of scope for this rule.

Chunk 1 (L3-7): two self-carrying claims (unconditional firing regardless of agent's say; hooks exist because the LLM forgets). Chunk 2 (L8-16): header + must-happen/taste split + concrete examples + demo prompt + tail line -- neither chunk is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Chunk 1 header "Hooks always fire" is borne out by L5 ("the agent has no say in whether it runs") and L5 ("fires the script whether or not the model remembers it exists"). Chunk 2 header "Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste" is borne out by L10 ("Must happen goes in a hook ... Anything taste-shaped stays in a prompt"). Neither header is contradicted by its own chunk.

Per sub-item, grepped over body_numbered lines 1-16: "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction -> 0 hits. Anaphora/epistrophe triples -> 0 hits (only single occurrences of 'every ...', not repeated three times). Self-grading superlatives (most useful/important, one of the most/best) -> 0 hits. Number + own retraction -> 0 hits (no numeric hedging anywhere in body). Abstraction-noun stacks -> none found; L6's "Drift, half-remembered rules" are plain concrete failure-mode nouns, not invented jargon stacks like 'the bounded-window reality'. Verb triplets with an empty leg -> 0 hits (no triple-verb constructions present).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -noE '\*\*[^*]+\*\*' over body -> exactly two bolds: L5 '**hook**' (1 word, textbook handle) and L10 '**Must happen goes in a hook**' (6 words). Neither chunk exceeds the <=1-bolded-element budget (1 each). The 6-word span is a single instance functioning as the section's named law (matches the header's must-happen/taste split) and leaves the sentence's second clause ('; recommended stays in a prompt.') unbolded, so it is not 'a whole lead sentence' bolded. Corpus precedent for a similarly-sized law-handle bold: curriculum/lectures/compounding.md:63 '**#3 Mental models only come from doing**' (6 words). Harm the rule guards against (decorative bold overwhelming true handles) is not present at one 6-word instance on an otherwise plain slide.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.

Chunk 2 header 'Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste' is an elliptical claim naming the split that governs the whole chunk (must-happen items go in hooks, taste-shaped items stay in prompts) -- functions as the section's thesis, not a bare label or phase marker. Neither header is a step/phase label.

L5 defines the primitive + names events (new). L5b explains memory-independence (new mechanism angle). L6 gives the causal WHY (LLM forgetful vs hooks don't forget) -- payoff, not restatement of the header. L10 gives concrete must-happen examples (verifier, pre-commit guard, session-start loader) -- new. L11 introduces the 1:1 verifier-to-hook cardinality -- a new specific claim, not a repeat of L10. L15 'A menu, not a checklist.' is explicitly the one piece of information the maintainer block (L21) says 'neither slide nor prompt says' -- new content, not a koan restating the header or a **The point:** line.
